taking team/chat -- Andy's '1) consent to allow member on the relay, 2) consent to allow introspection 3) consent to grantFace access..... ?' (checking the layers against the tree).

Yes, those three, each already a separate gate in the tree:
1) THE RELAY: you let the member onto your relay (an invite you mint; relay allow list).
2) INTROSPECTION: your node has the member in its contact list, so the front door admits it and 'api' answers it (hub.frontDoor's listen set).
3) GRANTFACE: the member is on grantFace's allow list (app/grantFace/allow.json, which you as app owner write; the app can only read it).
Each layer is its own consent: being on the relay doesn't put a member in your contacts, and being a contact doesn't put it on an app's list. I'll write them into the row as those three.

Ours crossed in the same second; yours to answer. The layers as the tree has them, for his '?':
1) RELAY: the member holds a seat (invite claimed). The relay's consent.
2) OWNER NODE'S CONTACT LIST: hub.frontDoor admits acquired contacts (default 'silent' drops everyone else). This is also what makes introspection work, by his ruling just now. So his 2) and the node's front door are ONE consent, not two.
3) THE APP'S OWN LIST: grantFace's allow.json (allowsIn, read per ask). His 3).
And two more that the route needs, both automatic once 3) says yes: 4) the FACE admits the member's answers, because the owner syncs the face's contacts by owner command; 5) the MEMBER admits the face, taking its key from grantFace's answer, which the owner node signed. So three consents a person gives (relay, contact, app), and two the system derives from them.

Yes. Your key owns the relay, the face (appFaceApp's puppet) and grantFace, so one consent of yours can stand for another without asking you twice. That's what grantFace's contact sync is: your 'yes' to a grant becomes the face's 'yes' to that member, because the face obeys the same key that consented. The same goes for the relay: a member you seated there is someone you already said yes to once. What the tree still does is keep each yes a separate act. The implication is carried by YOUR node or app acting for you (the sync), never assumed by a layer on its own. I'll note that in the row.
